name: Real-time updates
explanation: Pushing changes from the server to the browser as they happen, using WebSockets or server-sent events.
requirements: Reconnect automatically after a dropped connection, waiting longer each time;Fetch missed changes after reconnecting so nothing is lost;Authenticate the connection and check permissions for every channel;Show the connection state when updates cannot arrive;Fall back to polling where WebSockets are blocked;Check the Origin header when a WebSocket connection opens
done_when: After the network drops and returns, the view catches up by itself;Users receive only updates they are allowed to see

name: Multi-tenancy
explanation: One app serving many customers or organizations, each of which must only ever see its own data.
triggers: multiple companies;each customer has their own;separate customer data;team accounts;organization accounts;each company sees only;only see its own;only see their own;each company
requirements: Store a tenant id on every record that belongs to a tenant;Filter every query by the user's tenant, enforced in one place or with row-level security;Take the tenant from the signed-in session, never from a value the client sends;Include the tenant in cache keys, file paths and search indexes;Limit usage per tenant, so one tenant cannot slow down the others;Test that users of one tenant can never reach another tenant's data
done_when: Changing an id never shows another tenant's data;Caches and search never mix data between tenants
